tagline: Along the South Dakota line from Valentine to the Missouri.
intro: NE 12 leaves Valentine through the Fort Niobrara National Wildlife Refuge and keeps within ten miles of South Dakota nearly all the way east. It passes Sparks and Springview and Butte, crosses the Niobrara River into the village of Niobrara, and goes on through the Santee Reservation and Crofton, near Lewis and Clark Lake, to Ponca and on toward South Sioux City.
The village of Niobrara has moved twice, first after a winter flood in 1881 and again after a court blamed silt built up by Gavins Point Dam for ground water damage there.

moments.title: Smith Falls
moments.text: Reached by an old iron truss footbridge over the Niobrara, the state's highest waterfall drops 63 feet into a cool canyon where paper birch and aspen hang on from the ice age.

moments.title: Monowi
moments.text: When Rudy Eiler died in 2004, his wife Elsie became the whole village, its mayor, clerk and librarian, and she issued herself the liquor license.

moments.title: Ponca State Park
moments.text: On the high bluffs over the Missouri north of Ponca, where Lewis and Clark noted the wild plum and gooseberry thickets in the summer of 1804.
